interface.title: SatVision Cerrado — Detecção de Vegetação (Dashboard Final)
interface.field: Remote sensing / land-cover change monitoring (Brazilian Cerrado deforestation)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory screening and quick quantification of satellite scenes; a teaching or prototype dashboard (UNIP APS 2025/2), not a production pipeline
interface.what_it_is_for: Mask the vegetation in an RGB satellite tile with a manual HSV threshold or an automatic ExG/Otsu threshold, show a (placeholder) ResNet18 vegetation-vs-deforestation call, and for Cerrado areas compare two years as a per-pixel gain/loss/stable heatmap with pixel, percent and hectare totals.

data.note: Bundled EuroSAT class folders under data/processed (AnnualCrop, Forest, HerbaceousVegetation, Highway, Industrial, Pasture, PermanentCrop, …) and synthetic Cerrado time pairs under data/multitemporal (area_001 = a vegetated patch cleared between 2020 and 2024; area_002 = a patch regrown). I also uploaded the test files Forest_1.jpg and AnnualCrop_1.jpg. The classifier checkpoint is untrained, so its prediction and confidence values (about 0.63–0.70 'vegetação' for every image) were treated only as a UI feature.

screens_never_reached: The manual labelling interface (marking scenes as vegetação or desmatamento to build a reference set): per the repository README it is a separate Streamlit app, app/rotulador.py ('streamlit run app/rotulador.py'), which this run did not start. Not exercised; the dashboard (streamlit_app.py) itself has no labelling control.
A 'desmatamento' prediction: every image I tried was classed 'vegetação' (the checkpoint is untrained), so the other prediction state never appeared.
The help tooltip on the Resolução espacial field: hovering the (?) icon showed nothing.
not_done: Manually label scenes as vegetation or deforestation: this lives in the separate app/rotulador.py app, which this run did not start, so it was not exercised.

Save the quantitative summary: only the heatmap PNG is saved, and on the server, not in the browser. browser_downloads stayed empty, so I could not open the saved file. The Resumo Quantitativo has no export.
Use the ExG/Otsu method for the two-date comparison: the heatmap and summary always use the HSV thresholds and ignored the method switch (screens/038.webp, screens/039.webp).
Treat the IA prediction as a result: the confidence numbers come from a randomly initialised ResNet18, so I only recorded them as a UI feature.

Bug: after a new upload or a change of image source, the sidebar sliders and method radio and the comparison selectors go back to their defaults on screen, but the server keeps the earlier values. For example, the radio reads 'HSV Manual' while the result reads 'Auto ExG (Otsu)', and the selectors read area_001 2020/2024 while area_002 2024/2020 images are shown (screens/016.webp, screens/060.webp). What is displayed cannot be trusted to match what is computed.
Comparing a year with itself (2024 vs 2024) gives an all-stable result with no warning (screens/047.webp).
